macros.AbstractEvidenceStatus: The audited $\pi_{0.5}$ selector obtains 27.5\% task-macro SR over all 50 tasks and improves over its uncorrected static mask by 2.2 points (95\% task CI [0.6, 3.9]). The current evidence supports the mechanism and a favorable GR00T storage--accuracy point, but not yet same-budget superiority across architectures.
macros.ConclusionEvidenceStatus: The final $\pi_{0.5}$ selector obtains 27.5\% all-task macro SR. It improves over the uncorrected static mask (25.3\%) by 2.2 points (95\% task CI [0.6, 3.9], Holm-adjusted $p=0.045$). Its 1.3-point difference from FP16 has CI [-0.5, 3.2] and Holm-adjusted $p=0.240$, so this comparison is competitive rather than superior. Same-budget controls must complete before supporting a causal superiority claim.
macros.IntroEvidenceStatus: The final $\pi_{0.5}$ selector obtains 27.5\% all-task macro SR. Its 1.3-point difference from FP16 has CI [-0.5, 3.2] and Holm-adjusted $p=0.240$, so this comparison is competitive rather than superior. Both uniform-W6 controls have complete audited coverage and are reported descriptively. The search-matched random and action-only controls remain excluded from superiority claims until their exact manifests reach full coverage.
